family: Function or tool selection with closed arguments
source: Mixed questions and speculative branches row of the build-spec pattern table
description: Measures whether one prefill-only request can assemble a tool call: one Choice over a tool catalogue that always carries an explicit none option, closed-enumeration Choices for arguments, Nouls for optional-argument presence, per-member Nouls for set-valued arguments, and applicability gate Nouls that can reject an otherwise correct tool. The catalogue in every case contains overlapping siblings, so the pick turns on one clause of the request rather than on topic, and argument states carry a distractor value of the same type as the gold value. The headline metric is exact match on the assembled call, meaning the tool id plus every argument that belongs to the gold tool; tool-only accuracy, argument-only accuracy, and abstention precision and recall over the none cases are reported separately. In the gated cases the tool the request asks for is still the gold tool and its argument questions still carry gold labels fixed by the state, even though a false gate means a caller would not place the call: the gate must never move those answers. No case here asks an argument question that belongs to a tool it does not select. Only three cases are abstention cases and each states its negation in words, so the abstention numbers are thin and the suite holds no hard abstention probe. The none option does not sit in a fixed slot, so abstention cannot be read off answer position. This suite does not measure execution, retrieval, calendar or currency arithmetic, free-text argument generation, or probability calibration; no gold label here requires computing a number or resolving a date.

cases.name: replacement-already-arrived-return-label
cases.rationale: The middle of a long account states that a working replacement already arrived, so only the return of the original faulty unit is left and neither a second replacement nor a refund is wanted.

request.state: Thread summary for account C-4102. On the second the customer bought a portable espresso machine and an accessory kit, which shipped separately. On the sixth she wrote that the machine leaked from the base on first use and sent photographs; the accessory kit was fine and she has kept it. A replacement machine was dispatched on the ninth and arrived on the eleventh; she has used it twice and confirms it works correctly, so nothing further needs to be sent out. On the twelfth she asked whether she should keep the faulty machine, and we said no. She has now written again: the box is taped up and waiting by her door, she does not want money back because the replacement is fine, and all that is left is getting the faulty one back to us at no cost to her.
